chapter: 1950s clubs, Savoy dates and the Detroit sound
title: Reading through the 1955 run of Savoy dates
summary: The interviewer reads off dates with Clarke, Wendell Marshall, Cannonball, Nat Adderley and others, showing why Jones seemed the house pianist.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Well just looking at that…Let’s just….It’s 19…this is 1955.
1955, March 30, Kenny Clarke, Ernie Wilkins, septet date with George Barrow—Detroiter?

Wendell, Kenny Clarke. May 31st , an Eddie Bert date with Wendell and Kenny Clarke. Here it is. July 14, "Presenting Cannonball Adderley.” That was with Paul Chambers and Kenny Clarke; hat was band. July 26, Nat Adderley with Jerome Richardson and Wendell Marshall and Kenny Clarke in the band. August 2, another Ernie Wilkins and flutes and reeds dates with Wilkins, Jerome Richardson, Frank Wess. August 4th, a trio date with you and Kenny Clarke and Wendell Marshall.
[It just goes] on and on and on.
September 1st, Eddie Bert date. September 29th, Donald Green’s debut with Frank Foster, Paul Chambers, and Kenny Clarke
It’s easy to see how someone would think I am the house guy.
I mean, this goes on. October 6th and 11th, Al Caiola date. The 28th of October “Opus de Funk” with Milt Jackson.
